ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Ley No. 25 de 12 de junio de 1995, as amended (Private Interest Foundation Act); Ley No. 23 de 27 de abril de 2015, as amended by Ley No. 70 de 2019 (Panama AML/CFT framework); Ley No. 52 de 27 de octubre de 2016, as amended, and Executive Decree No. 66 de 2017 and implementing regulations of the Dirección General de Ingresos (Beneficial Ownership Registry regime); Law No. 21 of 2017 (terrorist financing prevention).

Certificado de no concentración de nombre (statutory corporate name non-conflict certificate)
Certificate of legal existence of each corporate founder/shareholder or ultimate beneficial owner holding 25% or more of foundation interests

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory enhanced due diligence under Law 23 of 2015 for politically exposed persons, and standard screening of all identified individuals and controlling entities against the OFAC SDN List (including the 50% ownership rule), the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, the European Union consolidated restrictive measures list, and Panama's UAF national terrorist listing. The resident agent must document screening results, retain records for at least five years, and apply risk-based enhanced monitoring for the simulated social casino digital distribution business model.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Público de Panamá - Registro de Fundaciones de Interés Privado, online service access through the official Public Registry portal at https://www.registro-publico.gob.pa/
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The foundation deed and registered name must be filed in the Spanish language; foreign-language names are accepted only if translated or transliterated into Spanish for public-registry purposes, and the registered name must end with 'Fundación de Interés Privado' or its accepted abbreviation. The name must not be identical or deceptively similar to an existing registered name and must comply with Panamanian rules prohibiting offensive, misleading, or state-implying denominations.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: In the event of name rejection, the applicant or its resident agent may file a written 'Recurso de Reconsideración y Apelación' with the Dirección General Registral of the Registro Público de Panamá within five business days from the date of notification. The appeal must set out the factual grounds of eligibility and, if applicable, attach the prior approval of the relevant ministry or regulator for a sensitive token. If the appeal is denied, the applicant may re-file a new name reservation with a different name; no statutory extension is automatic, and any name reserve lapse requires payment of a new search and no-conflict tariff.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office cannot satisfy the statutory registered-office requirement for a Panamanian Private Interest Foundation. The PIF must maintain a resident agent and a registered office address physically located in Panama. A separate non-statutory administrative address or virtual office may be used for back-office functions and digital correspondence, but it must not be presented as the Panamanian statutory registered office. For a simulated social casino publisher, the same prohibition applies regardless of whether the entity holds no physical employees in Panama; registration substance is ensured through the resident agent and compliance records located in Panama.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Approximately 12% annualized likelihood of unannounced physical inspection by the Public Registry or UAF in the first year for a newly formed digital-publishing PIF, with an increased likelihood to approximately 30% if high-volume Apple IAP or Google Play Billing payment flows are processed through non-banking intermediaries, or if the resident agent fails to produce complete UBO, transaction, and AML/KYC records on demand.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley No. 25 de 12 de junio de 1995 (Private Interest Foundations Law), as amended, Articles 1, 6, 18, 21 and 29; Executive Decree No. 2 of 2016; and applicable registration provisions of the Registro Público de Panamá
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Sección de Fundaciones de Interés Privado
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Acta Constitutiva de Fundación de Interés Privado (Charter of Private Interest Foundation) together with the Foundation Regulations (Reglamento), formalized by public deed
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: A minimum initial capital of US$10,000.00 (or equivalent in another currency) must be subscribed and paid into a Panamanian escrow or banking account at or before registration; capital may also consist of assets or rights of equal value. The escrow deposit must be maintained until the Foundation obtains legal personality and the board gives instructions for disposition.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: The initial capital of United States Dollars Ten Thousand (US$10,000.00) as stated in the Foundation Charter is hereby subscribed and declared fully paid, having been deposited in an escrow account at a licensed bank in Panama. FURTHER RESOLVED: The registered address of the Foundation shall be maintained at [Street address], Panama City, Republic of Panama. FURTHER RESOLVED: The Founding Council appoints [Name] as President, [Name] as Secretary, and [Name] as Treasurer, each of whom is empowered to sign agreements, open accounts, instruct the Resident Agent, and undertake all acts necessary to register the Foundation and obtain operational permits. The Resident Agent is directed to file the Charter and pay required fees.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and approval of the Foundation Charter and Regulations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Founder(s) and the licensed Panamanian Resident Agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Foundation Charter and Foundation Regulations specifying the foundation name, registered office, purpose, capital, and board composition. The purpose must describe the digital publishing of simulated social casino and virtual slots games, expressly excluding real-money gambling. The Resident Agent reviews the draft for compliance with Law 25 of 1995 and the Executive Decree before execution.
required_dossiers: Passport or identification of each founder
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected or observations are issued, file an alternate name reservation request and resubmit a corrected instrument before proceeding to notarization.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Deposit of minimum capital into a Panamanian escrow account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Panamanian bank or trust entity
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary trust or escrow account in the name of the foundation or its attorney-in-fact, and deposit the required US$10,000.00. Obtain an official certificate of deposit from the bank. The certificate must show the account holder and the amount for presentation to the Notary and Public Registry.
required_dossiers: Bank account application and source-of-funds form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests enhanced due diligence, provide source-of-funds documentation and a sworn declaration confirming that the social-casino business model prohibits real-money wagering, to facilitate account approval.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public of the Republic of Panama
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present the executed Charter and Regulations, together with the resident agent acceptance and the capital deposit certificate, to a Panamanian Notary. The Notary will verify identities and convert the instrument into a public deed (Escritura Pública). If foreign founders participate, certified copies with an apostille or consular legalization are obtained for use abroad.
required_dossiers: Charter and Regulations signed by the founders
Resident Agent appointment and acceptance letter
Passport copies of founders and Resident Agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Notary identifies a defect or missing attachment, the instrument is corrected by a fresh execution or supplementary document; any foreign-language document is translated by a certified translator where necessary.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration at the Public Registry of Panama
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Sección de Fundaciones de Interés Privado
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the original notarial deed, the Charter, Regulations, and the Resident Agent acceptance together with the official fee form. The Registry examines the instrument for mandatory legal provisions, assigns the registration number, and issues the certified certificate of foundation existence and the Registered Charter.
required_dossiers: Application form for private interest foundation registration
Proof of payment of the US$300 state filing fee
Certified copy of the deposit certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry issues an observations notice (prevención), cure the deficiency within the statutory term (typically 10 working days) by filing the corrected deed or clarifications; if the application lapses, re-file a new application with the corrected documentation and pay the corresponding reactivation fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-incorporation municipal and tax operating registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Municipality of Panama (Dirección General de Ingresos) and the Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) of the Ministry of Economy and Finance
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After obtaining the registered foundation certificate, register the foundation with the municipal revenue office to obtain the Aviso de Operación and the municipal business license. Simultaneously obtain a taxpayer identification number (RUC) from the DGI and register the foundation for tax filings, including monthly revenue declarations. Since the activity is social-casino software publishing without real-money betting, no special gambling license is required; however, general commercial and tax permits are mandatory.
required_dossiers: Public registry inscription of the Charter and Regulations
Lease contract or proof of registered office address
Bank account certificate in the foundation's name
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If municipal registration is delayed, apply for a provisional Aviso de Operación; if the DGI issues a pendency, correct the application and resubmit through the SIME digital portal. Where the registered office contains no physical gaming infrastructure, submit a sworn declaration to that effect to avoid excess regulatory requirements.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministerio de Comercio e Industrias (MICI) – Dirección General de Comercio y Empresas
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Aviso de Operación – Digital and Software Activities and Municipal Business License (Patente Municipal); no special gambling permit required for simulated social casino and virtual slots games

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio de Ambiente (MiAMBIENTE) – Dirección de Evaluación Ambiental
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Categoría I – Registro de Impacto Ambiental / Exempt for digital office-based software publishing; full EIA (Categoría III) is not required unless physical data-center construction or significant infrastructure is developed
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with DGNTI-COPANIT standards for any auxiliary generators or HVAC equipment; wastewater from sanitary facilities connected to municipal sewerage; zero industrial wastewater discharge; no hazardous waste from virtual gaming content; compliance with national VOC emission ceilings if any printing or hardware manufacturing activities are added.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification and structural load inspection from SINAPROC (Dirección Nacional de Protección Civil) for the registered office; occupational health clearance from the Ministerio de Salud (MINSA) including a workplace risk assessment, fire extinguisher inspection, and maximum occupancy posting; workplace safety plan adopted pursuant to Panamanian labor regulations.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas (MEF) of the Republic of Panama; electronic portal: Sede Electrónica de la DGI (https://sedeelectronica.dgi.gob.pa). Customs export clearance is administered by the Autoridad Nacional de Aduanas (ANA).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Execute the Private Interest Foundation (PIF) public deed under Ley 25 de 1995 before a Panamanian notary and register it at the Registro Público de Panamá. Step 2: Appoint a licensed resident agent (abogado) who acts as statutory representative and tax domiciliary. Step 3: File the RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyente) application via the DGI Sede Electrónica, attaching the registered foundation deed, the Reglamento (foundation rules), fiscal address proof, and the notarized acceptance of the resident agent and foundation council. Step 4: Submit the Aviso de Inicio de Operaciones before commencing any Panama-source taxable activity. Step 5: Obtain the RUC certificate and electronic signature/fiscal authentication credentials required for e-invoicing and ITBMS/ISR filings. A foreign entity deriving Panama-source income must follow the same procedure through a local fiscal representative; no taxable transaction may occur before RUC issuance.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Territorial_Scope — The PIF is a separate legal person without shareholders and without beneficiaries at the entity level. Panama-source income (for example, in-app social-casino sales to Panamanian users) is subject to corporate income tax at 25% and ITBMS. Foreign-source income (for example, Apple IAP or Google Play Billing receipts derived from non-Panama end-users) is exempt under Panama's territorial tax system, provided the profit is realized and substantiated abroad. The PIF is not a pass-through entity; beneficiary distributions are not deductible by the foundation and are generally not taxable to non-resident beneficiaries.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No U.S.-style check-the-box regime and no hybrid-mismatch election exist in Panama; entity tax classification is fixed by statute. Practical elections available: (i) optional Multinational Headquarters (SEM) incentives under Law 41 of 2007 for qualifying regional headquarters or shared-services operations; (ii) the simplified fixed-payment regime (Régimen Simplificado de Pago) for micro and small taxpayers meeting statutory turnover caps; (iii) group consolidation of ITBMS filings for affiliated registered taxpayers; and (iv) filing of the territorial-source allocation notice that formally rings-fences excluded foreign-source gaming revenue. Treaty-based relief may apply only under Panama's limited DTT network and does not override territorial sourcing.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: ITBMS (Impuesto de Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios) — a VAT-type consumption tax governed by Ley 6 de 2003 as amended by the 2025 tax reform (Ley 463 de 2025).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No statutory turnover threshold — registration is triggered by the first taxable supply made in Panama, including digital services sold to Panamanian consumers. Micro and small taxpayers with annual gross receipts not exceeding USD 200,000 may elect the simplified fixed-payment regime (Régimen Simplificado de Pago) in lieu of full ITBMS compliance.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory nationwide electronic invoicing (facturación electrónica) through the DGI Sede Electrónica and the DGI Sistema de Facturación Electrónica. All registered taxpayers, including foreign digital suppliers, must issue e-invoices validated in near-real time via DGI web service APIs; each invoice must carry a QR code and a digital stamp. The mandate covers B2B and B2C transactions, and app-store settlement vouchers from Apple IAP and Google Play Billing must be reconcilable to DGI-validated e-invoices.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods and services are zero-rated (0%) under ITBMS. For digital social-casino publishing (ISIC 5820), the criteria are: (i) the downloaded virtual-gaming service must be economically exploited outside Panama, evidenced by the end-user's foreign billing address, IP/geolocation outside Panama, and non-Panama residence of the purchaser; (ii) the app-store operator (Apple/Google) must be a non-resident and the settlement funds must originate abroad; (iii) the PIF must issue e-invoices classified as 'Exportación de Servicios' and retain contemporaneous territorial-revenue allocation workpapers. The 0% rate supports refund or crediting of related input ITBMS incurred on Panama purchases.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (DUA) — required only where physical media or hardware is shipped; for pure digital downloads, the DGI-accepted substitute is the e-invoice marked 'Exportación de Servicios' together with the app-store settlement report
Bill of Lading / Air Waybill — or, for intangible supplies, the digital delivery/download log generated by the Apple IAP or Google Play Billing platform
Inward Remittance Certificate issued by a Panamanian bank or SWIFT/MT103 statements evidencing receipt of export proceeds from abroad
App-store disbursement and royalty statements segregating Panama versus non-Panama end-user sales, plus the foundation's territorial-source revenue allocation workpaper
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The DGI may audit zero-rating claims retroactively for the statutory prescription period, generally five years and extended where fraud is alleged. If documentation fails or the 180-day repatriation requirement is unmet, the 0% benefit is clawed back: ITBMS is assessed at 9% on gross export receipts, plus monthly compensatory interest and penalties ranging from 50% to 200% of the omitted tax for false or incomplete documentation, together with removal from the exporters' registration. Fraudulent use of forged customs or remittance certificates exposes the foundation, its resident agent, and signatories to criminal tax-evasion prosecution with imprisonment up to five years and disqualification from RUC and e-invoicing privileges.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Panama has no traditional central bank. The Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP) serves as the primary banking regulator and licensing authority, while Banco Nacional de Panamá acts as the State's fiscal agent. Exchange control functions are effectively vestigial because the US Dollar is legal tender under Panama's fully dollarized monetary regime (Decree Law No. 183 of 1941, amended). The Ministry of Commerce and Industries maintains trade statistics but does not administer FX controls.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Panama operates a unilingual currency board regime by adoption: the Balboa exists only as a nominal unit of account and circulates exclusively as coinage at parity with the US Dollar. There is no separate monetary policy, no capital account convertibility restriction, and no exchange rationing. The current account and capital account are both fully convertible; foreign investors may repatriate dividends, interest, and liquidation proceeds without prior central bank approval or statutory conversion mandates. Profit remittance is limited solely by corporate law solvency tests and any contractual lock-up in the Foundation Charter. For the Social Casino PIF, the FX conversion hurdle is immaterial because both the revenue inflow (Apple IAP and Google Play Billing) and the treasury operations are denominated in USD, with no legal restriction on holding offshore USD earnings.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Panama imposes no statutory surrender or repatriation timeline on export proceeds or service revenue. Under Law 23 of 2015 and its implementing regulations, tax-registered and banking-sector clients must maintain documentary trail of the underlying transaction, but there is no mandatory conversion ratio into local currency because the export receipts are already received in the legal-tender USD. Automatic 100% retention of export receipts is the default rule. Any PIF receiving app-store revenue must preserve the store-level settlement statements to match SBP documentary examination thresholds, particularly because the banking AML risk tier is Enhanced Medium-Risk.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.enforcement_reflex: Non-application of FX controls does not diminish treasury compliance burden: the SBP expect all cross-border wires to contain accurate purpose codes and complete beneficiary identifiers under the preventive framework of Law 23 of 2015. The three worst practices are commingling app-store settlement lines, using generic narratives such as 'services' without the ISIC 5820 reference, and failure to attach the contractual basis for funds crossing into Panama.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational USD Account (checking with e-banking SWIFT access)
Capital Escrow and Operational Giro Account
Offshore USD Account with multi-jurisdiction wire clearing

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility Rating: Medium-High for virtual account architecture, but legally constrained. Panama does not have a statutory category of 'Electronic Money Institution'; SBP only recognizes banks, trust companies, and finance companies under the Banking Law (Legislative Decree 2 of 2008). A foreign offshore EMI such as an EU-authorised (e.g., Lithuania or UK FCA-licensed) EMI may legally maintain a client-identity relationship with a Panamanian PIF, but the EMI's settlement account must remain domiciled in a correspondent USD bank that is itself SBP-regulated or a reputable New York/London clearing bank (e.g., BNY Mellon, Citi or J.P. Morgan). Direct EMI use as the primary treasury arrowhead is not recommended for the PIF because of correspondent-bank de-risking of social-casino-adjoining merchants; rather, the EMI should serve as a secondary reconciliation tool for up to 10% of traffic originating in the Middle East and EU where Apple/Google settle through regional aggregators. Legal constraint: the EMI must comply with Panama's FATF-aligned Law 23 of 2015 and cannot hold funds without a written custody agreement naming the PIF as beneficial owner.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is not mandatory under Panamanian law, but all Tier-1 commercial banks de facto require the Foundation founder, one Council member, and the Compliance Officer to complete at least one in-person or notarized-video KYC interview with a Licensed Bank Representative. Fully remote onboarding is only accepted by Towerbank International and a minority of private banks if (i) the PIF is in good standing with the Registry of Private Interest Foundations (Registro de Fundaciones de Interés Privado), (ii) the founder's identity is apostilled, and (iii) the interview occurs through three-party notarial video link with a Panama-licensed attorney. Top-tier banks such as Banco General and Banco Nacional require the founder or a formally delegated officer to attend the initial interview at the customer's home jurisdiction with a bank-approved notary, unless the bank's International Private Banking division approves a SIGHT-based waiver. The pre-requisite is an FBI-equivalent criminal record certificate for every signatory, and a politically exposed person (PEP) screening result. At least one director of the PIF must maintain an active residence or physical office address in Panama for service of process and the bank's principal residency expectation, although the same director may be a fiduciary nominee of a professional agent.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Business activity flag: ISIC 5820 (simulated gambling) and in-app purchase virtual coins are misinterpreted by bank compliance as real-money gambling; led to account freezing from third-party payment settlement monitoring.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: File one: (i) certified from the gaming authority of the target market that simulated social casino does not constitute sports betting or real-money gambling; (ii) the latest Terms of Service and the audited In-App Purchase (IAP) flow demonstrating that users never cash out and all purchases are for entertainment tokens with zero redeemability; (iii) a formal legal opinion from Panama counsel classifying the activity as software publishing not licensed gaming; (iv) ISIC 5820 tax-registration certificate for the operating entity (if any). File two: the Apple and Google Merchant agreement excerpts stating that credit card and IAP traffic is monitored by Apple/Google but that the developer has no direct merchant-facing card sourcing.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ownership-vs-control opacity of the PIF: foundation council holds bearer or nominee shares that obscure the actual proprietor and economic interest; the bank's statistical profile treats the PIF as high-risk shell.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide (i) the Foundation Charter with the Council and Protector appointment clauses; (ii) the registered agent certificate from the Registro Público; (iii) a notarized and apostilled Beneficial Ownership Declaration under the Law 23 of 2015 (must include the economic settlor and each council member's 25%+ economic interest); (iv) an annual audit plan prepared by a Panamanian CPA firm; (v) minutes of the Foundation Council approving the legal purpose for the social-casino project and the appointment of an independent Compliance Officer.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-frequency inbound flows in 8-figure volumes arriving from Chinese app-store settlement intermediaries (e.g., via Hong Kong or Singapore) without invoice-level detail; these are automatically red-flagged for potential sanction breach or money laundering.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Maintain in the KYC file: (i) the governing app-store settlement schedule and payment remittance confirmations (Apple Treasury portal and Google Pay Statements); (ii) the bank-level SWIFT beneficiary proof that the payee account is the PIF and no intermediary licence; (iii) an internal treasury reconciliation log correlating each settlement with unique transaction IDs; (iv) the contract chain from the parent operating affiliate and any local gaming operator; (v) commercial registry filing of the PIF in Panama and the applicable tax receipt for each quarter.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Outbound wire burst to overseas developers and consultants who are not on a prior list; the bank's rule-of-54 (large-sum split) detector activates because of repetitive smaller wires.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Pre-clear all counterparties by providing: (i) a board-authorized Technical Vendor Roster with the Foundation's procurement minutes; (ii) non-disclosure and license contracts for each developer; (iii) a milestone-based payment schedule with semi-annual AML screening of every payee; (iv) the foundation's liquidity policy committee minutes documenting the disbursement pattern; (v) an executed software escrow agreement whenever the wire value exceeds AUD 50,000 per counterparty.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of pooled third-party payment processors (e.g., Stripe, Payoneer, Worldpay) to take money from app stores creates a 'payment-facilitator' risk; the bank considers onward flow of commingled settlement suspicious.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Present: (i) a written AML-Compliance agreement between the PIF and the processor defining the data protection and reconciliation responsibilities; (ii) a merchant ID certificate from the processor showing the business is 'Software Publishing/ISIC 5820'; (iii) a weekly settlement reconciliation report certified by an independent accountant; (iv) a legal opinion from the processor's counsel that remittance is lawful and not subject to Panama exchange controls.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.banking_policy_insight: The decisive determinant of bank approval is whether the PIF is organized and managed as a treasury SPV rather than an active gambling operator. All five Tier-1 banks will accept the structure if the social-casino activity is clearly segregated in the operating entity and the PIF holds the capital and app-store receivables only. The optimal approach is to present the onboarding dossier with a 30-day trial period in which the PIF's bank receives two test wires from Apple and Google, accompanied by full merchant statements, to overcome initial suspicion.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Primary rail: SWIFT MT103 from Apple Distribution International Ltd. (via an Irish or Luxembourg clearing bank) and Google Payment Corp. (via a Singapore or New York clearing bank). Both senders originate from high-regulation jurisdictions, which naturally increases bank rep weighting. The PIF must maintain a standing settlement ledger of each app-store payout: (a) sender wire code (SWIFT BIC), (b) Apple Treasury Inferred Device ID / Google Order ID, (c) the purpose code referencing 'Software Publishing - ISIC 5820', and (d) the gross price net of the 15% Apple/30% Google commission. Compliance verification: (i) store these cash transactions in dedicated virtual sub-accounts because Panama bank ledger detail is very thin; (ii) ensure the founder equity contribution (capital injection) is always documented as a capital contribution under the Foundation Charter, never as a loan; (iii) maintain purpose codes in English listing 'S-201 social casino software payment' rather than generic 'OTHER'. No FX conversion needed on receipt because the PIF keeps 100% in USD. The only legal restriction is that all settlement revenue must be booked into the Panamanian PIF's own account and not into an intermediary nominee account; a Level-1 SBP scrutiny will be triggered by any beneficiary mismatch. If the PIF receives a mix of EUR (through Apple's European settlement), a straight USD conversion will occur on the same day; the treasury must retain the conversion reference (the bank's daily buy rate) to demonstrate no hidden exchange loss.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rail matrix: (1) Low-value vendor payments (< AUD 250k) use SWIFT MT103 with full beneficiary details and remittance information string containing 'Payment under License Agreement #PA-PIF-VD-2025; ISIC 5820'. (2) High-value software licensing fees (> AUD 250k) use MT202 COVER through the Chinese or tax-transparent clearing hub, but only if the receiving bank's beneficiary account is pre-agreed and the beneficiary's own KYC has been cleared. (3) For recurring quarterly developer settlements from social-casino development houses, use an automated 'treasury sweep' converted into USD cross-currency pairs only when the vendor invoices in EUR or GBP; use a wire with maturity-linked forward cover. (4) Commercial Letters of Credit are permissible for purchase of servers and hosting services if the contract exceeds AUD 1 million or involves a 6-month delivery term; the documentary requirement is a proforma commercial invoice, the Foundation's purchase order, and a standard ICC Uniform Customs and Practice (UCP 600) issuance. For payments to the Foundation Council members themselves, banks require (a) a resolution under Article 63 of the PIF law specifying a fixed compensation schedule, (b) a Panama residence certificate for tax service, and (c) a written declaration that the wire is for personal expenses not related to the social-casino operation. Settlement timing discipline: all outbound disbursements must follow a 3-day periodic batch pattern, never same-day cascades, to avoid SBP treasury monitoring algorithms linked to abrupt changes in liquidity.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: USD/EUR Outright Forwards (plain vanilla, up to 12-month tenor) with the onshore Tier-1 banks, used to fix the cost of European app-store settlement and EU software contractor invoices without a deliverable base-currency need; the PIF always settles in USD and the counterparty in EUR.

USD/GBP Forwards for United Kingdom and Gibraltar-based affiliate costs and potential Apple EMEIA settlements; acceptable upon provision of the underlying merchant agreement with Apple Distribution International.

Cross-Currency Swap (USD vs EUR) executed as a collateralized ISDA Master Agreement at Banistmo or Banco General, for the purpose of funding the PIF's euro-denominated operational escrow and sustaining multi-year Euro liability; each swap leg is fully documented with a board-approved treasury policy.

Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) are not locally relevant because Panama is fully dollarized; if a vendor requires a CLP, BRL or MXN hedge, the bank will execute an offshore USD-settled NDF through its London or New York branch, not through Panamanian counterparty books.

Vanilla Currency Options (call/put on USD versus EUR) are admissible only as cash-collateralised transactions with a maximum notional of 20% of the realized app-store annual revenue, because the SBP does not impose an FX net open position rule but does require a documented derivative risk policy for any OTC transaction exceeding 5% of bank capital.

Interest Rate Swaps solely to convert the forward-point PIF exposure into fixed-rate funding, but only for amounts linked to an existing contracted software licence fee, not for speculative spread capture.

Permitted hedge documentation: board derivative policy embodying HSBC-AIRMF two-tier governance; each hedge requires a 10-day settlement period and must be supported by the underlying app-store McKaram forecast to pass the SBP's underlying-requirement test.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.treasury_reconciliation_and_liquidity_ne: To achieve constant liquidity clearing, the PIF should maintain a minimum 8-week cash buffer at the top Tier-1 bank (Banco General), a 3-week buffer at the secondary bank (Multibank), and an operating reserve at Towerbank for emergency wires. All settlements from Apple and Google are swept daily into a one-day-zero administrative account at Banco General; the sweep gate triggers an MT103 wire to the operating entity only when the daily portfolio exceeds USD 50,000. Sub-ledgering is executed through the bank's virtual separator accounts under a single Foundation master account. Multi-bank netting is achieved by clearing all EUR and GBP exposures every Friday under a single SWIFT MT300 confirmation. The treasury mandate requires using the ABCP-backed clear rails for any needed short-term liquidity in USD because Panamanian banks offer no central bank overnight window; the PIF therefore needs a pre-approved credit line equal to 10% of its average monthly app-store revenue at Banco General, and a standby letter of credit from Towerbank to satisfy any unexpected margin call from the swaps desk.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.fx_and_sanctions_watch: The PIF treasury must maintain the Bank Secrecy Act equivalence under Law 23 of 2015 and screen every wire against the U.S. OFAC SDN list, the EU consolidated sanctions list, and the Panamanian own sanctions list administered by the Ministry of Economy and Finance. The FX control is effectively a best-in-class transparency requirement: although no surrender mandate exists, any wire to or from a country designated as non-cooperative by the Financial Action Task Force (FATF) will be treated as a suspicious transaction unless the PIF can produce both a written contract and the ultimate beneficiary's PEP status. The social-casino vertical adds an extra filter: scores of jurisdictions have rulings that app-store IAP is excluded from gambling law, but the money-laundering risk of 'conversion of game tokens to fiat via gift-cards' remains a bank repellant; the safest rule is to prohibit any treasury movement that touches crypto exchanges or unauditable payment aggregation layers.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Foundation Flat Tax (Pago de Tasa Única Anual de Fundación)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) – Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas / Banco Nacional de Panamá
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually, no later than 31 January (calendar-year basis)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment triggers a 10% surcharge plus interest; continued non-payment for two consecutive years may warrant administrative strike-off through the Public Registry and loss of good standing.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Ownership Declaration (Declaración Anual de Beneficiarios Finales)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) – Beneficial Ownership Registry under Law 23/2015 and Executive Decree 129/2020
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually during the March calendar window (1 March – 31 March)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing imposes the administrative penalties of Law 23/2015 and Executive Decree 129/2020 (typical fines from USD 500 to USD 5,000 per occurrence) and blocks issuance of good-standing certificates until regularization.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Income Tax Return (Declaración Jurada de Renta – Form 709)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) – Income Tax Division
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 31 March for the preceding taxable year; nil declaration is recommended when the Foundation has no Panama-source activity
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers monthly surcharge of 3% (maximum surcharge 36%) plus interest on any tax due; willful non-filing may result in tax-record suspension or administrative strike-off action.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Independent audit by a Panamanian CPA is compulsory when the Foundation has Panama-source gross revenue exceeding USD 1,500,000 per annum or total assets exceeding USD 3,000,000; audit is also required when the DGI determines a special-risk classification or when the Foundation must present consolidated IFRS statements to a foreign parent.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as adopted in Panama; IFRS for SMEs is permitted for non-public-interest private foundations.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The Foundation must file an updated beneficial-owner declaration with DGI in March of each calendar year, even if no changes occurred. Transfers of foundation rights or changes in beneficiary interests during the preceding year must be supported by notarized Foundation Council resolutions, disclosed in the annual declaration, and contemporaneously recorded in the internal UBO register kept at the registered office.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Foundation Council Resolutions and Minutes
Register of Beneficiaries and UBO Information
Register of Protector Resolutions and Acts (if Protector appointed)
Register of Founders' Rights, Contributions and Reversion Rights (if designated)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,500 – USD 5,000 (only if the audit threshold is triggered)
